# HELICOBACTER PYLORI INFECTION

H. pylori infection is associated with peptic ulcers, gastritis, gastric adenocarcinoma, and gastric lymphoma. Antimicrobials should be given to patients with confirmed H. pylori infection. Antisecretory therapy should be given concurrently.

Test of cure should be completed at least 4 weeks after completion of therapy (recommended within 4-8 weeks after completion). Any PPI therapy must be held for 2 weeks prior to testing.

Lab H. Pylori, stool

Note: American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) advises adult household members of individuals who have a positive non-serological test for H. pylori to seek testing trough their provider.

*Local guidance (St. Cloud CDSS, Inpatient):*
*Provider to place order: Lab H.pylori, stool
*Requires Prior Authorization Drug Review
Amoxicillin/Omeprazole/Rifabutin (250/10/12.5MG) 4 caps po tid x14days[DI]

---

References:

- Chey et al. ACG Clinical Guideline: Treatment of Helicobacter pylori infection. Am J Gastroenterol, 2024, 119(9):1730-1753.
- VA PBM Clinical Recommendations November 2024. Use of newer combination products in the treatment of H. pylori infections.
- Mandell chapter: Helicobacter pylori and Other Gastric Helicobacter Species
- Sanford Guide article: Gastric/Duodenal Ulcer, Helicobacter pylori
- Up-to-Date article: Treatment regimens for Helicobacter pylori
Therapy:
## First line treatment:

Bismuth subsalicylate 524 mg PO q6h <AND> Tetracycline 500 mg q6h DI

<AND> metronidazole 500mg PO q6h [DI] <AND> omeprazole 20mg po q12h.

Take all for 14 days.

## Alternative treatments:

Alternatives may have lower efficacy and higher resistances rates. Test of cure extremely important.

**_Consider referring patients who cannot take first line therapy to GI pharmacist for treatment management and follow-up testing._**
Gastroenterology (OP) Consult - Pharmacists

## Rifabutin triple (Talicia):

Note: place medication order and PADR using order below
Amoxicillin/Omeprazole/Rifabutin (250/10/12.5MG) 4 caps po tid x14days DI,H

< OR >

## PCAB dual (Voquezna DualPak-Amoxicillin/Vonoprazan):

*Requires Prior Authorization Drug Review
PCAB Dual (vonoprazan 20mg q12h/amoxicillin 1000mg q8h) po x14daysDI
per package instructions

< OR >

## Clarithromycin Quadruple:

Resistance to clarithromycin is increasing. Do not use for patients with prior exposure to macrolides. Consider susceptibility testing prior to use.

Clarithromycin 500 mg PO q12h R,DI <AND> Amoxicillin 1000 mg PO q12h R

<AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h [DI] <AND> omeprazole 20 mg PO q12h.

Take all for 14 days.

*Local guidance (St. Cloud CDSS, Inpatient):*
<AND> metronidazole 500mg PO q6h [DI] <AND> omeprazole 20 mg PO q12h. Take all for 14 days.
